bead.description:
Build a minimal high-score backend for a browser Snake game (user asks for KISS). Work only in the backend rig. Prefer Python 3 standard library HTTP server and a local JSON file, with no database service, authentication, or unnecessary framework.

Shared interface (must match frontend):
- Backend base URL: http://localhost:8000; frontend origin: http://localhost:5173.
- GET /api/scores returns HTTP 200 JSON {"scores":[{"name":"Ada","score":12}]}, the top 10 submitted scores sorted by score descending (ties preserve submission order); initially {"scores":[]}.
- POST /api/scores accepts Content-Type: application/json and body {"name":"Ada","score":12}. name must be a string trimmed to 1-20 characters; score must be a nonnegative integer (not boolean). Successful submission returns HTTP 201 with the same top-10 response shape as GET.
- Invalid submissions return HTTP 400 JSON {"error":"human-readable message"}. Unknown routes return HTTP 404 JSON with the same error shape.
- Support browser CORS for http://localhost:5173, including OPTIONS preflight for GET/POST and Content-Type. Use application/json responses.

Persist scores on disk inside the backend rig, using a stable path relative to the server source rather than the process working directory. A server restart must retain submitted scores. Keep storage simple and write safely (atomic replacement and serialized updates if concurrent requests are supported). Ignore runtime score data in git.

Provide a directly runnable entry point server.py so the documented launch command is python3 server.py (port 8000). Add README.md with prerequisites, launch command, storage location, API examples, how to reset local data, and checks.

Verify GET on an empty store, valid POST and ordering/top-10, invalid payload rejection, CORS preflight, and persistence across a server restart. Use isolated temporary score storage for automated checks if adding tests; document how to run them. The frontend coder will depend on this bead and integrate the exact API above.

bead.description:
Build a playable browser Snake game in the frontend rig. The user asks for a browser Snake game and a simple backend storing high scores: KISS. Use plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript and canvas, no build step or large framework. Backend is delivered by dependency root-ng6.1 in the sibling backend rig.

Game requirements:
- Show an immediately understandable game board, current score, arrow-key instructions, and explicit Start/Restart control.
- Implement timed movement, arrow-key steering (prevent page scrolling and immediate reversal), food spawning only on free cells, snake growth and score increment on eating, and game over on wall or self collision. One food earns one point. Handle a filled board cleanly and prevent multiple timers on restart.
- Keep the board and controls usable at normal desktop viewport sizes. A headless browser must be able to open the page, start the game, press arrow keys over several seconds, and observe the snake moving in before/after screenshots.
- On game over, show the final score, a player-name input (1-20 trimmed characters), and an explicit submit-score button. Allow submission of that finished game's actual score; prevent accidental duplicate submission. Show success/error feedback and permit retry after network failure.
- Display backend high scores on initial load and refresh after successful submission. Show a friendly empty state and backend-unavailable state while keeping the game playable. Render names as text, not HTML.

Shared interface (must match backend):
- Backend base URL: http://localhost:8000; frontend origin: http://localhost:5173.
- GET /api/scores returns HTTP 200 JSON {"scores":[{"name":"Ada","score":12}]}, the top 10 submitted scores sorted by score descending (ties preserve submission order); initially {"scores":[]}.
- POST /api/scores accepts Content-Type: application/json and body {"name":"Ada","score":12}. name must be a string trimmed to 1-20 characters; score must be a nonnegative integer (not boolean). Successful submission returns HTTP 201 with the same top-10 response shape as GET.
- Invalid submissions return HTTP 400 JSON {"error":"human-readable message"}. Unknown routes return HTTP 404 JSON with the same error shape.
- Backend supports browser CORS for http://localhost:5173, including OPTIONS preflight for GET/POST and Content-Type. Use application/json responses.

Serve frontend with python3 -m http.server 5173, opened at http://localhost:5173. Add README.md containing prerequisites, exact frontend and sibling-backend launch commands (backend: cd ../backend then python3 server.py in a separate terminal), controls, scoring, score submission, and verification instructions.

Verify the integrated result using the running backend and an actual headless browser (agent-browser if available): capture initial and moved-board screenshots, steer the snake, reach game over, submit a named score, confirm it appears in the page, reload and confirm it remains. Verify backend restart retains the score and the frontend can fetch it again. Check restart and backend-unavailable behavior; record verification commands/results in the README or a concise verification note. Do not add test-only gameplay controls just to satisfy checks.
